slides.headline:
The star stayed in Shanghai.
The kitchen came to Jeju.
slides.subline: Yong Fu, Jeju Shinhwa World — the first Korean dining room from Shanghai's MICHELIN-starred Ningbo house

slides.label: when Yong Fu opened its first restaurant in Korea, at Jeju Shinhwa World
slides.note: The Shanghai original, Yong Fu (Hongkou), holds One MICHELIN Star in the MICHELIN Guide Shanghai 2026. The Jeju dining room is the group's first in Korea and is not itself starred. Sources: guide.michelin.com, The Korea Herald

items.d: A port city south of Shanghai. Its food belongs to the Jiangnan tradition — seafood-led, restrained in seasoning, built on slow braising

items.t: Salt and time rather than chilli
items.d: Salted and cured seafood is a Ningbo signature. The Shanghai flagship has live white crab and yellow croaker shipped in daily from the East China Sea
Weng Youjun opened Yong Fu to push Ningbo ingredients into fine dining. The group now runs restaurants across Shanghai, Beijing and Hong Kong
Yong Fu (Hongkou) carries One MICHELIN Star in the Shanghai 2026 guide, and the Hong Kong outpost, open since 2019, holds one as well

slides.title:
Two islands
sharing one pantry.
slides.body:
A luxury Chinese restaurant inside a Korean resort usually means Peking duck and a nice view. The reason this one is worth a second look is narrower than that: Ningbo cooking is defined almost entirely by the East China Sea — abalone, crab, croaker, cured and braised rather than fried hot.

Jeju is an island with the same argument about itself. Its food identity is its own sea, plus black pork. So the signature dishes the Korean press listed at opening are the overlap rather than an import: braised abalone in Ningbo-style sauce, a spicy stir-fry of Jeju black pork, chilled marinated crab.

One honest note. The MICHELIN star belongs to the Shanghai dining room, not this one — the group brought its recipes to Jeju, not its rating. Whether the cooking travels is a separate question, and not one we can answer for you.

items.t: Marriott building, G floor, Jeju Shinhwa World
items.d: 38 Sinhwayeoksa-ro 304beon-gil, Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo, Jeju. Restaurant phone +82 64-908-1240
Hours as listed on the resort's own dining page. Booking through shinhwaworld.com or Catchtable
The Korea Herald reported a 48,000-won lunch set and a 78,000-won dinner set per person at opening in May 2025. À la carte is served as well

items.t: What the press listed as signatures
items.d: Braised abalone in Ningbo-style sauce, spicy Jeju black pork stir-fry, chilled marinated crab, Peking duck, Dongpo pork and dim sum

slides.by:
We have not eaten here. Whether the food justifies the trip across the island is your call, not ours.
Prices, hours and menus change without notice — confirm before booking.

caption:
A Michelin-starred Shanghai seafood house quietly opened its first Korean kitchen on Jeju.

Yong Fu arrived at Jeju Shinhwa World in May 2025, cooking Ningbo dishes with Jeju abalone and black pork. Lunch sets from 48,000 won.

The star is Shanghai's, not this room's, and we haven't eaten here.

Sources in the last slide.
